title: Temporary access code serves as identifier
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest could serve as a unique reference to identify the data subject's access event, potentially linking the guest to the home access.
assumptions: The access code is logged and stored by the system

title: Access code retention beyond functional need
description: The temporary access code may be stored longer than functionally needed for unlocking the door, creating unnecessary data retention risk.
assumptions: The system logs and stores access codes for audit or future reference

title: Sensitive access data collected
description: The access code is a sensitive piece of data that may be more sensitive than strictly required for the simple function of unlocking a door.
assumptions: The access code is treated as personal data

title: Guest unaware of data processing
description: The guest may not be fully aware of how their access code is being collected, stored, or processed by the Home Hub system.
assumptions: No clear privacy notice or consent mechanism is provided

title: Potential violation of data minimization
description: Processing the access code may exceed what is functionally needed for the simple door unlocking function, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: GDPR or similar regulations apply to this system

title: Linking through unique identifier in motion alert
description: The motion alert may contain device identifiers or user identifiers that could be used to link the motion event to a specific individual or device.
assumptions: Motion alerts typically include device/user identification for routing and attribution purposes.

title: Quasi-identifier combining through motion data
description: Motion data combined with timestamp and location context could serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to individuals.
assumptions: Motion alerts contain timestamp and location context that, when combined, could identify individuals.

title: Processing of identified data in motion alert
description: The motion alert may contain unique references to the identity of the data subject (e.g., user ID, device ID).
assumptions: Motion alerts are typically associated with specific users/devices for notification purposes.

title: Revealing attributes in motion data
description: Motion data may reveal revealing attributes such as location, time of activity, and movement patterns that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Motion alerts inherently contain contextual information about when and where motion occurred.

title: Data type sensitivity - motion data may be more sensitive than needed
description: Motion data could be perceived as highly sensitive (revealing presence, location, activity patterns) and may be collected/processed beyond what is strictly required for the alert functionality.
assumptions: Motion alerts are used for security monitoring but may reveal more about user behavior than necessary.

title: Data propagation to other services
description: Motion data may be propagated to other services or systems where it is not functionally needed for the alert purpose.
assumptions: The mobile app backend may share or store motion data for analytics or other purposes beyond the immediate alert.

title: Unawareness of processing as data subject
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their motion data is being collected, transmitted, and processed by the home hub and mobile app backend.
assumptions: Users may not be informed about the extent of motion data processing and sharing.

title: Lack of control over motion data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their motion data is processed, collected, or shared.
assumptions: Users may not have granular control over motion data processing settings.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (motion data) may be processed than is actually needed for the functional goal of sending a real-time motion alert.
assumptions: Motion data collection may exceed what is necessary for the alert functionality.

title: Linking through unique identifier in notification
description: The motion-detected notification likely contains the homeowner's unique identifier (e.g., user ID, phone number) to route the notification to the correct recipient, enabling linking of the notification to a specific individual.
assumptions: The notification includes identifying information to deliver to the correct homeowner.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in motion data
description: Motion detection data may include location, time, and device information that can be combined to create a quasi-identifier, potentially linking the notification to the homeowner's specific activities and location.
assumptions: Motion detection data includes location and timestamp information.

title: Identifier in notification routing
description: The notification system processes identifiers (user ID, phone number) to route the motion alert to the correct homeowner, making the data identifiable.
assumptions: The system uses unique identifiers to deliver notifications to specific homeowners.

title: Revealing attributes in motion detection
description: Motion detection data reveals revealing attributes such as time of day, location, and activity patterns that can support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Motion detection includes timestamp and location data.

title: Detection through observed communications
description: The notification itself reveals that motion was detected at a specific time and location, making the event observable to the homeowner and potentially others.
assumptions: The notification is sent to the homeowner's device and may be visible to others.

title: System response reveals motion event
description: The system response (sending the notification) reveals that motion was detected, which could be used to infer the homeowner's presence or activities.
assumptions: The notification is triggered by motion detection and sent to the homeowner.

title: Excessive data granularity in notification
description: The notification may include more granular location or time data than functionally needed for simply alerting the homeowner about motion.
assumptions: The notification includes precise location/timestamp data.

title: Unnecessary data treatment and enrichment
description: Motion detection data may be analyzed, enriched, or processed beyond what is needed for the simple notification functionality.
assumptions: The system may analyze motion patterns beyond basic notification needs.

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware that their motion detection data is being collected, processed, and transmitted to the backend system.
assumptions: Privacy policies may not clearly disclose motion data collection.

title: Lack of control over motion data preferences
description: The homeowner may have limited control over how motion detection data is processed, stored, or shared.
assumptions: Limited user controls for motion data preferences exist.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data (motion data, location, timestamps) than is actually needed for the notification functionality.
assumptions: Motion data collection exceeds functional requirements for simple alerts.

title: Linking through unique video identifiers
description: Video clips stored in the DataStore may contain unique identifiers (e.g., file IDs, timestamps, or metadata) that can be used to link the video to a specific homeowner or account.
assumptions: Video metadata includes identifiers that can be correlated with user accounts

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Video metadata may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., timestamp, location, device ID) that when combined can uniquely identify the homeowner.
assumptions: Video metadata includes multiple attributes that can be combined to identify individuals

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The video clip is associated with a specific homeowner account, making it identified information that is processed for playback.
assumptions: Video is linked to homeowner identity through account association

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content may reveal identifying attributes about the homeowner (e.g., appearance, location, activities) that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Video content captures identifiable information about the homeowner

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is inherently sensitive personal data that may be collected and stored beyond what is strictly necessary for basic playback functionality.
assumptions: Video data is more sensitive than other data types and requires careful handling

title: Unnecessary video processing
description: Video data may be processed, analyzed, or enriched in ways not necessary for simple playback (e.g., metadata extraction, analytics).
assumptions: System may perform additional processing on video beyond playback

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Video data may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary (e.g., cloud storage providers, analytics services, support teams).
assumptions: Video data is shared with multiple service providers and internal teams

title: Unawareness of video processing
description: Homeowners may not be fully aware of how their video data is collected, stored, processed, or disclosed by the system.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all video processing activities

title: Lack of control over video preferences
description: Homeowners may lack control to set preferences regarding how their video data is processed, stored, or shared.
assumptions: Limited user controls for video data management

title: Lack of control over video rectification/erasure
description: Homeowners may lack the ability to easily rectify incorrect video data or request deletion of video data that is no longer relevant.
assumptions: Video deletion or modification processes may be complex or unavailable

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data may be processed in excess of what is actually needed for the playback functionality, violating data minimization requirements.
assumptions: GDPR and similar regulations require data minimization

title: Potential invalid consent for video processing
description: Video data collection and processing may not rely on valid, informed consent from the homeowner.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may be unclear or not properly obtained
